title: Weak equivalences glue through double mapping cylinders
statement: Use the path components and the continuous cubical homotopy groups of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], spelled out here for arbitrary topological spaces: for a space $X$, $x\in X$ and $r\geq1$, $\pi_r(X,x)$ is the group of homotopy classes relative to the boundary of continuous maps $([0,1]^r,\partial[0,1]^r)\to(X,x)$, with multiplication by concatenation in the first coordinate. A continuous map $h:X\to Y$ is a weak homotopy equivalence if it induces a bijection from the path components of $X$ to those of $Y$ and, for every $x\in X$ and $r\geq1$, a group isomorphism $h_*:\pi_r(X,x)\to\pi_r(Y,h(x))$, $h_*[u]=[h\circ u]$. For continuous maps $f:C\to A$ and $g:C\to B$ of topological spaces put $$D(f,g)=(A\amalg(C\times[0,1])\amalg B)/((y,0)\sim f(y),\ (y,1)\sim g(y)),$$ with the product and quotient topologies. Let $f':C'\to A'$, $g':C'\to B'$ be a second such pair and let $e_A:A\to A'$, $e_C:C\to C'$, $e_B:B\to B'$ be continuous maps with $e_Af=f'e_C$ and $e_Bg=g'e_C$. Then $e_A\amalg(e_C\times1_{[0,1]})\amalg e_B$ induces a well-defined continuous map $D(e):D(f,g)\to D(f',g')$; this assignment satisfies $D(1)=1$ and $D(e'e)=D(e')D(e)$ for composable such triples. If $e_A$, $e_C$ and $e_B$ are weak homotopy equivalences, then $D(e)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. No Hausdorff, compact generation, connectedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed; any of the spaces may be empty.

proof.text: Write $I=[0,1]$, $D=D(f,g)$ and $D\prime=D(f\prime,g\prime)$, and let $q:A\amalg(C\times I)\amalg B\to D$ be the quotient map. The map to $D\prime$ given on the three summands by $a\mapsto[e_A(a)]$, $(c,t)\mapsto[(e_C(c),t)]$, and $b\mapsto[e_B(b)]$ is continuous. At $t=0$ the two identified representatives have images $[f\prime(e_C(c))]=[e_A(f(c))]$; the $t=1$ check uses $e_Bg=g\prime e_C$. Thus it is constant on the generating identifications and factors uniquely through the quotient as a continuous map $E=D(e)$. The identity triple has the identity formula on every representative. For composable triples, both $D(e\prime e)$ and $D(e\prime)D(e)$ send $[a]$, $[(c,t)]$, $[b]$ respectively to $[e_A\prime e_A(a)]$, $[(e_C\prime e_C(c),t)]$, $[e_B\prime e_B(b)]$. Surjectivity of $q$ gives the asserted functoriality.

proof.text: Define $L=q(A\amalg(C\times[0,2/3)))$ and $R=q((C\times(1/3,1])\amalg B)$. Their full inverse images under $q$ are exactly the displayed summands (with empty contribution from the omitted endpoint summand). They are open and saturated in the disjoint union, so $L,R$ are open in $D$ and cover it. Restricting a quotient map to the inverse image of an open target subset is again quotient: openness of an inverse image for the restriction is openness in the full source, and the quotient criterion applies. Consequently $L$ and $R$ carry precisely the quotient topologies of these truncated cylinders. Their intersection $T=L\cap R$ has no endpoint representatives; its full preimage is $C\times(1/3,2/3)$, where there are no identifications, so restriction of $q$ gives a homeomorphism $C\times(1/3,2/3)\cong T$. Make the same definitions $L\prime,R\prime,T\prime$ for $D\prime$. Since $E$ preserves the interval coordinate on interior points and sends each endpoint summand to the corresponding endpoint summand, $E^{-1}(L\prime)=L$, $E^{-1}(R\prime)=R$, and $E^{-1}(T\prime)=T$.

proof.text: There is a continuous retraction $r_L:L\to A$, given by $r_L[a]=a$ and $r_L[(c,t)]=f(c)$; its continuity follows by descent from the two continuous summand maps and the quotient description of Step 2. Let $i_A:A\to L$ be the canonical map. Then $r_Li_A=1_A$. On $L$ use $H_s[a]=[a]$ and $H_s[(c,t)]=[(c,(1-s)t)]$ for $0\leq s\leq1$. These formulas respect the endpoint identification, stay in $L$, and give $H_0=1_L$, $H_1=i_Ar_L$. Here joint continuity for the quotient topology requires justification: on $Q_L=A\amalg(C\times[0,2/3))$ the formulas define a continuous map $Q_L\times I\to L$. By [lem-coef-compact-open-currying], with the locally compact interval $I$, its transpose $Q_L\to\operatorname{Cont}(I,L)$ is continuous. Identified representatives have identical paths, so the transpose descends continuously along the quotient $Q_L\to L$ to $L\to\operatorname{Cont}(I,L)$. Evaluation, by the same cited statement, gives the continuous homotopy $H:L\times I\to L$. Thus $i_A,r_L$ are homotopy inverse maps, using $H_{1-s}$ and the constant homotopy on $A$ for the reverse orientation.

proof.text: For $R$ define $r_R[b]=b$, $r_R[(c,t)]=g(c)$ and $i_B(b)=[b]$. The homotopy fixing $B$ and sending $[(c,t)]$ to $[(c,1-(1-s)(1-t))]$ runs from $1_R$ to $i_Br_R$, stays in $R$, and respects the $t=1$ identification. The two summand formulas are continuous before quotienting; transpose into $\operatorname{Cont}(I,R)$, descend through the open restricted quotient of Step 2, and evaluate as in Step 3, using [lem-coef-compact-open-currying]. Hence this too is a continuous homotopy inverse pair. Under $T\cong C\times(1/3,2/3)$ let $r_T$ be projection to $C$ and $i_C(c)=(c,1/2)$. The homotopy $(c,t,s)\mapsto(c,(1-s)t+s/2)$ gives $1_T\simeq i_Cr_T$, while $r_Ti_C=1_C$; continuity is ordinary product continuity and the coordinate remains in $(1/3,2/3)$. These constructions use only the two given continuous maps, so they apply verbatim with $f\prime,g\prime$ to give the three primed homotopy inverse pairs.

proof.text: Assume now that $e_A,e_C,e_B$ are weak homotopy equivalences. By [lem-coef-homotopy-equivalence-weak], all six retractions $r_L,r_R,r_T,r_{L\prime},r_{R\prime},r_{T\prime}$ are weak homotopy equivalences, since Steps 3-4 provide their continuous homotopy inverses and the homotopies (reverse the homotopies there when needed). The formulas give exact equalities $r_{L\prime}E|_L=e_A r_L$, $r_{R\prime}E|_R=e_B r_R$, and $r_{T\prime}E|_T=e_C r_T$. At any $x\in L$, the first equality on homotopy groups reads $(r_{L\prime})_* (E|_L)_*=(e_A)_*(r_L)_*$, with basepoints $x,E(x),r_L(x),e_A(r_L(x))$ and $r_{L\prime}(E(x))=e_A(r_L(x))$. All factors other than $(E|_L)_*$ are isomorphisms, so it is an isomorphism. The identical equation on path-component sets makes $E|_L$ bijective there. The second and third equalities give the same conclusions for $E|_R$ and $E|_T$. This argument uses only postcomposition on representatives and cancellation of bijections or group isomorphisms; no change-of-basepoint or connectedness assumption is needed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-open-cover-weak-equivalence] to $E:D\to D\prime$ and the target open cover $D\prime=L\prime\cup R\prime$ from Step 2. Its three inverse-image restrictions are exactly $E|_L,E|_R,E|_T$, which Step 5 proves are weak homotopy equivalences. The cited theorem therefore makes $E=D(e)$ a weak homotopy equivalence. It allows arbitrary spaces, including empty intersections and empty source or target, so it applies without imposing any separation or compact-generation hypothesis. In particular when $C=\varnothing$, $L=A$, $R=B$ and $T=\varnothing$; if $A$ or $B$ is empty the existence of $f$ or $g$ forces $C=\varnothing$. The formulas and retractions above still hold on empty summands.
